headline: Jagex, the maker of RuneScape, pulled a game trailer and apologised after fans said it looked AI-made and showed a character with six fingers.
score_reason: Pool score kept: the takedown and apology were reported on 5 Oct 2026 by several outlets, but it is a gaming-community story with no wider effect.
importance_line: Players who raised concerns about suspected AI-made art twice in a few days now have Jagex's promise of tighter checks on its partners' work, but the studio has not yet said how the trailer was made and admits its own review let it through.
summary: PC Gamer reports that Jagex, the developer of the online game RuneScape, took down a trailer for its upcoming Dragon Slayer 2 quest and apologised after fans said footage shown at its RuneFest event over the weekend looked AI-generated, pointing to a character with six fingers. Jagex says it is investigating, that the outside partner behind the trailer had promised not to use generative AI, and that this is the second such concern in days, after a clothing collaboration with 100 Thieves; it adds that it is overhauling its review process.
notes: Trailer debuted at RuneFest over the weekend (3-4 Oct 2026); the apology is reported on 5 Oct 2026 by PC Gamer, Kotaku, IGN and games.gg (statement time not given), so freshness is NEW. Jagex's Reddit statement is the primary source, quoted alike by PC Gamer and Kotaku.
